title: Biased Fourier coefficient identity
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p_i\in(0,1)$ for each coordinate $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $S$ be a set of coordinates. The Fourier coefficient of $f$ against the product of the standardized biased signs on $S$ equals the product of their standard deviations times the sum, over all coordinate sets $T\supseteq S$, of the ordinary Fourier coefficient on $T$ weighted by $\prod_{i\in T\setminus S}(1-2p_i)$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$S$ is a finite set of coordinates
